nogueira-silva.name: Nogueira da Silva Museum
nogueira-silva.short: A patron’s house museum on Avenida Central: art from the 15th to the 20th century and a French-style garden
nogueira-silva.long: The businessman and collector António Nogueira da Silva bequeathed his house, garden and collection to the University of Minho in 1975. The house was built in the 1950s and 1960s to a design by Raul Rodrigues Lima. Inside are paintings, furniture, silver, Chinese porcelain, ivory and tapestries. Behind the house lies a garden with box-hedged parterres, statues and tiles.
nogueira-silva.history:
António Augusto Nogueira da Silva (1901–1976) was born in Porto into a bourgeois Braga family; his relatives traded in wool and worked in banks. His fortune came from the Casa da Sorte, a lottery office he opened in Braga in 1933. Branches later spread across Portugal and the colonies. Even before the 1974 revolution he handed the firm over to its employees.

Nogueira da Silva gave generously to the city. He built a neighbourhood with a school, finished the Congregados basilica and helped found the Catholic University. In 1964 Braga made him an honorary citizen. The house on Avenida Central was designed by Raul Rodrigues Lima, the architect of cinemas and courthouses. It was built in two stages, in the 1950s and the 1960s, and planned for large receptions.

In September 1975 Nogueira da Silva bequeathed the house, garden and collection to the University of Minho, and in 1976 he died. He bought the pieces in the 1960s at auctions and from antique dealers. What to look for in the rooms: a painted 15th-century Italian cassone chest, Chinese export porcelain made for the European market, and a 17th-century Luso-Mughal ivory plaque. The main Portuguese painting is André Gonçalves’s Last Supper. The house also holds a contemporary art gallery, a photo library and an art history library.

The garden is laid out in the French manner: parterres framed by box hedges, magnolias and a Baroque fountain from an old manor house in Gualtar. Among the greenery stand ceramics by Jorge Barradas, two 18th-century Dutch tile panels and a 19th-century copy of Bernini’s Apollo and Daphne.
facts: The house, garden and collection were bequeathed to the University of Minho in September 1975.
The house was built in the 1950s and 1960s to a design by Raul Rodrigues Lima.
The rarest piece is a painted 15th-century Italian cassone chest.
Nogueira da Silva paid for the west tower of the Congregados basilica.
The Baroque fountain in the garden was brought from an old manor house in Gualtar.
nogueira-silva.tip: The museum stands at Avenida Central 61, almost opposite the Congregados basilica. Check opening hours and prices on the museum’s website: it is usually closed on Sundays, Mondays and public holidays. After the rooms, be sure to step out into the garden.
